items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split the orchestrator effects into separate threat rows**

This task changes trust-boundary review rules, but its threat table combines merge, update-branch, and forced removal in one row. The newly established unit requires one row per orchestrator effect, so these three controls must be independently dispositioned rather than grouped; otherwise the task violates the exact completeness rule this commit adds.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/9b2c02a1a8763816b8774914541c6fef47e9f2a9/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit the mapping check to invariant-bearing tasks**

The new fixed stop condition unconditionally requires every task ID to occur in the design's `implementing_tasks` and have matching invariant IDs. This commit's own `kind: docs` task has no `invariants` field and `dotfiles-T128-playbook-rules-a01` is absent from the referenced design's map, so applying the rule literally makes this task—and other non-implementation docs/review tasks—impossible to approve. Qualify this check for tasks that actually claim design invariants.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Search the correction index instead of raw correction text**

The mandated lookup cannot reliably determine whether a matching correction exists. For the existing repeated class `bookkeeping`, both prescribed searches return no matches even though `M-20261012-4.md` links the failure to corrections C-3 and C-6; conversely, searching the existing class `sources` makes `grep -rl` return every correction because each file has a generic `sources:` field. This can incorrectly force creation of a duplicate correction or select an unrelated one, so the procedure should query the mistake/index mapping or require an explicit class field in correction records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add class fields before searching them**

Fresh evidence after the earlier correction-search finding is that the amended head still has no `classes:` field in any of the 14 files under `.orchestration/learning/mistakes/` (`git grep '^classes:' ee2d5e1 -- .orchestration/learning/mistakes` returns no matches). Consequently, when an S1 class reaches three, this prescribed command always reports no match and the following rule incorrectly requires creating a duplicate mistake and correction instead of following the existing `corrections:` links; add/populate the class index in the same changeset or search an existing source that actually maps ledger classes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define a wall-clock trigger for stalled-result checks**

When a worker goes silent after reading a TASK, “past the task's expected duration” has no computable threshold: the message contract supplies only `max_turns`, and step 7 merely says to track that turn count, which cannot advance or be observed while no messages arrive. The failure mode this sentence is intended to prevent can therefore still result in an arbitrarily long silent wait; define a concrete elapsed-time limit or add an explicit duration field to TASKs before requiring the bus read and PING.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Land the gate check before claiming S6 enforcement**

In this commit's tree, `scripts/require-crit-review.py` never reads `ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE`, and the Makefile does not forward it, so when a finding class reaches three the documented gate command can still succeed without any acceptance record or pasted correction search. The added token test only verifies this sentence, not the merge backstop; either land `dotfiles-T128-gate-evidence-a01` first/in this changeset or avoid stating that the gate refuses the action.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/c4e0bb72ab045b8a9d4d013fa2c4eacdc5c3589b/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Implement C4 before relying on its threat-row check**

This commit says C4 mechanically verifies every `allowed_files` row before dispatch, but the reviewed tree contains no task-consistency checker implementation—only prose/tests containing its name—and the checked-in learning index still records `task-consistency-check C4` as pending. Consequently a task can omit an allowed-file threat row while reviewers are told that this half is already verified; land the validator with this rule or keep the check explicitly manual until it exists.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/c4e0bb72ab045b8a9d4d013fa2c4eacdc5c3589b/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle partially landed correction statuses**

When the search resolves to C-2, the prescribed branch is ambiguous because `.orchestration/learning/corrections/C-2.md:13` records `status: "landed for fixtures and the bullet; pending for C4 and T701"`, rather than either state this procedure recognizes. Treating it as landed applies a correction whose validator is still absent, while treating it as pending gives no definition of which remaining mechanisms must land; define partial status handling or normalize correction records to the two states before making this the acceptance procedure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the complete bus before rebuilding open tasks**

When more than 20 messages follow an open task, the shown `history.sh <team>` read omits its TASK because that CLI defaults to the latest 20 rows, a limitation already documented in `.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-regime-counters-a02.md:28-29`; the governing design likewise requires a storage-facade or explicit-`--limit` read at `.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-regime-v3-a01.md:172`. After a compaction, rebuilding the open-task list from the truncated view can therefore drop active work and produce false status or duplicate dispatches, so this procedure needs to require a complete-history read.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Measure stalls from the latest task event**

Fresh evidence in this amended head is that the new fixed-duration clause tests whether any seat event occurred since the TASK, rather than measuring inactivity since the latest relevant event. A worker that sends one early PONG and then goes silent—or emits an event for an older task while this task is stalled—will always have “a bus event from its seat since,” so the 30-minute condition never becomes true and no PING is required; reset the inactivity clock from the latest event for this task.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize the class before executing search commands**

When this path is triggered by `scripts/regime-counters.sh`, the class is derived from the first three words of a review-comment title with no shell-safe normalization (`scripts/regime-counters.sh:143-147`). Such a title can contain backticks, `$()`, apostrophes, or other metacharacters; substituting it into the unquoted `memory search <class slug>` command can execute text on the orchestrator host, while an apostrophe also breaks the single-quoted grep pattern. Require a defined `[a-z0-9-]` normalization or safely pass the value as a quoted argument rather than interpolating review-derived text into shell commands.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/fe34f7db0311fd5503104abe1a4b8ddec509c547/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match complete class values in the correction lookup**

Fresh evidence in the amended head is that the prescribed lookup still conflates distinct classes: for the existing S1 class `scope`, `grep -rl 'classes:.*scope' .orchestration/learning/mistakes/` returns both records whose class is `scope` and `M-20261012-3.md`, whose class is only `class-count-scope`. Because the next step follows every returned record's correction IDs, a substring collision can surface unrelated corrections or make a class with no exact record appear to have a match; parse the YAML list or require delimiter-aware exact matching.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile counter candidates with slugged classes**

Fresh evidence in the amended head is that the two trigger paths still use incompatible class formats: `scripts/regime-counters.sh:145-147` emits the first three title words verbatim (the existing unit test expects `class=reject skipped contract`), while this rule requires the triggered class to be a `[a-z0-9-]` slug assigned during disposition. When that counter path reaches three, “search for that class” therefore supplies a non-slug with no defined mapping to the ledger class, so the required manual validation/search cannot proceed. Make the counter emit the assigned slug or explicitly resolve its candidate against the disposition ledger before searching.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use INV-10's 20-minute idle threshold**

For a seated worker that emits no task event for 20–29 minutes, this rule delays the bus read and PING even though `.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-regime-v3-a01.md:64` explicitly limits worker idleness to 20 minutes. INV-10's 30-minute figure applies to the first-push deadline, not idle detection; align this sentence and the referenced `bus-read.sh` behavior with the 20-minute threshold.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define threat rows per concrete changed path**

When an `allowed_files` entry is a permitted wildcard such as `scripts/orchestrator/*`, one generic row now satisfies the stated unit even if the PR changes several independently executable trust-boundary scripts. The existing T718 task demonstrates why the distinction matters: its single wildcard covers `dispatch.sh`, `three-repeat.sh`, and `bus-read.sh`, which require three different controls. Defining completeness per concrete changed file, or forbidding multi-file globs at trust boundaries, prevents a broad entry from hiding missing threat analysis.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/7771082f7db20a6ea1b53c5e95817aee6e23e177/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare invariant sentences as well as IDs**

For an implementation task that carries the correct invariant IDs but weakens or replaces their text, this stop condition passes even though `.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T128-regime-v3-a01.md:56` requires task invariants to equal the trusted design both as an ID set and byte-for-byte as sentences. Because the worker receives and follows the task copy, checking only IDs can dispatch work against a modified contract; require each invariant value to match the design in addition to matching the map entry.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
